subject: Climate & Environment
title: Pumped Hydro Storage
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pumped Hydro Storage usable.

hook.text: The world's largest battery isn't made of lithium. It is made of water and gravity.

buildup.text: When power is cheap, pumps push water uphill into a reservoir. It waits there.

discovery.text: When demand peaks, the water flows back down through turbines, generating electricity.

twist.text: Pumped hydro accounts for 90% of all grid-scale energy storage worldwide.

climax.text: Some systems use old mines or underground caverns instead of hilltop reservoirs.

punchline.text: Gravity never runs out and never needs a software update.

quiz.question: What share of global grid-scale energy storage is pumped hydro?

details.summary: Pumped hydro storage is the oldest and largest form of grid energy storage. It works by pumping water uphill to a reservoir when power is abundant and releasing it through turbines when demand peaks. Pumped hydro accounts for over 90 percent of global installed energy storage capacity.
details.whyItMatters: Pumped hydro provides large-scale, long-duration storage that batteries alone cannot yet match economically. It stabilizes grids and enables higher renewable integration.
takeaways: Pumped hydro provides over 90 percent of grid storage worldwide
Water is pumped uphill during surplus and released during peaks
Round-trip efficiency is typically 70 to 85 percent

faq.question: Where can pumped hydro storage be built?
faq.answer: It requires two reservoirs at different elevations connected by pipes and turbines. Mountainous terrain and old quarries or mines are ideal. Closed-loop systems that don't connect to natural rivers reduce environmental impact and expand suitable locations.

faq.question: Is pumped hydro still being built?
faq.answer: Yes. Countries like China, Australia, and India are building large new pumped hydro facilities. Australia's Snowy 2.0 project will provide 2,000 megawatts of storage. Globally, hundreds of gigawatts of capacity are in planning or construction.
